_doc: Surgical per-effect corrections, merged by tools/preprocess.mjs AFTER parseEffectsFromDesc (PRE-P12-DATA-QUALITY.md §3). Keyed overrides.<resonatorId>.<slotKey>, where slotKey is 'S<level>.<index>' (chain) or 'IH<node>.<index>' (inherent). Only the listed fields change; the parser output is the base. Special fields: suppress:true drops the effect; an entirely new slotKey adds an effect the parser missed (supply a full effect object). Every slotKey must reference a real slot (data-integrity tested).

IH0.0._resolvedVia: 2026-07-31 gauge-engine increment 3: 'When casting Basic Attack: True Sight - Conquest or Basic Attack: True Sight - Charge, each stack of Enflamement will increase Fusion DMG Bonus by 5%.' The value clause names neither a cap nor a stack source because both live in her Forte Circuit text: 'Changli can hold up to 4 stacks of Enflamement' + 1 per True Sight Conquest/Charge hit, 4 per Resonance Liberation, all consumed by Heavy Attack Flaming Sacrifice. Modelled as RESOURCE_DEFS[1205] 'Enflamement'; the stackTrigger reads that gauge's per-step level. The trigger was 'unknown' (so the effect was entirely OFF), fixed to the two casts the kit names - same skillKeys shape as her S2.0 override. Window is 'thisCast': the bonus applies to that cast, so 'persist' is wrong in both directions - its castMatch check reads strictly EARLIER steps, missing the very cast the buff is for and then applying to every step after it.

S6.1._resolvedVia: 2026-10-03: the clause names FIVE skills in a SUBJECT list -- "Galbrena's Basic Attack - Seraphic Execution, Heavy Attack - Flamewing Verdict, Mid-air Attack - Hellsent Barrage, Resonance Skill - Ravage, and Dodge Counter - Purgatory Scourge gain 0.875% Fusion DMG Amplification, up to 35%" -- and the subject binder deliberately never reads across a comma (that is how it avoids binding a team buff to the trigger list in front of it), so it bound NOTHING and the surviving skillType 'basic' is dead: her kit reads no basic bucket. Her sibling S6.0 names FOUR of the same skills in a TARGET form ("the DMG Multipliers of X, Y, Z ... are increased"), which the binder DOES read, and resolved them to the ten keys copied here -- so these eleven are S6.0's own resolved list plus Ravage, not a fresh derivation. A CATEGORY-NAMED buff scopes the ABILITY, not the damage bucket (maintainer, 2026-10-03): "a buff can apply to a certain ability/mechanic directly, which in turn buffs that ability's DMG without the buff having to be explicitly of the proper DMG type" -- which is why a NAME scope is right here and matching the attribution would be wrong. Dodge Counter - Purgatory Scourge resolves to NO key (her only dodge-counter row is "Blood for Blood"), so it is a named-but-unreachable skill and is simply absent, understating by one move. STILL OFF, deliberately: the stack source is "for every 1 point of Afterflame consumed" and Afterflame is not modelled. It IS identifiable -- SpecialEnergy2, cap 40, matching "Galbrena can hold up to 40 points of [Afterflame]" with no other channel reading 40 -- but its income is "+8 when Resonators in the nearby team cast Echo Skill" (trigger row 1208003100, amount 8), which is the HIT/EVENT lane rotation-resources.js cannot read and is team-composition dependent: the same blocker as Sigrika's Innate Gift?. So this override fixes the SCOPE only; the effect still resolves OFF via its unknown trigger, which audit-effects.test.mjs tracks as UNKNOWN_TRIGGER.

IH0.0._resolvedVia: 2026-10-03 (OPEN-ITEMS 2, the "ICD-gated enemy debuff"): Oathbound Hunt had trigger AND stackTrigger both 'unknown' and a scope of skillType 'skill' that NO hit of hers can read, so it was dead three times over. The VALUES were already right from the parser (perStack 0.05, maxStacks 4, stackSeconds 5.5) — only the stack SOURCE and the scope were missing. SCOPE: "Each stack Amplifies the DMG directly dealt by Galbrena's Normal Attack, Resonance Skill, Forte Circuit, Resonance Liberation, Intro Skill, and Outro Skill" is a MECHANICAL list of inputs, not a list of damage buckets, and the game's own ROW LABELS are what resolve it: the leading category of a label is the move's KIND and a trailing · Forte Circuit is provenance. Read as buckets the clause would be nearly inert — her kit reads only heavy/echo/intro/outro, so four of the six named categories have no hit at all. Read by label it omits exactly ONE category, Heavy Attack, excluding all six Heavy keys (plain Volley of Death AND Forte Flamewing Verdict) and admitting the other 21. That is why the list is written instead of "all her damage", and why "Forte Circuit" is in it rather than redundant: it is the catch-all for Hellstride and Hellsent Barrage, whose labels lead with Forte Circuit rather than another category. Both Heavy Attacks TRIGGER the stack and do not benefit from it, which is coherent. STACKS: TARGET_STACK_DEFS[1208] 'Fated End' — the ICD is per LISTED SKILL, not per category (maintainer-confirmed: "each same skill may only apply 1 stack every 5 secs; using different skills in succession builds the stacks much quicker"). The kit's closing sentence proves it: Encroach and Ravage are both mechanically Resonance Skills reading the Heavy bucket, so "considered the same type of skill" says NOTHING under a per-category reading and real work under a per-skill one. WINDOW kept as parsed ('seconds' 5.5, the stack lifetime) and armed by the applying casts: a stack applied by the last listed cast expires exactly when the window does, and a cast whose group is still on ICD opens the window while the count is 0, which pays 0. The count is what gates this effect, exactly as Denia's per-Dark-Core multiplier is gated by arithmetic.

S6.1._scopedVia: 2026-10-02, CORRECTED after review: the clause states NO damage category at all. Its only occurrence of "Resonance Liberation" is the first two words of the skill's own proper name, "Resonance Liberation Rewritten in Winter’s Margins" — the parser lifted that into skillType 'liberation' as a FALSE POSITIVE off the NAME, not as a second statement about damage type. The kit grants 40% DMG Bonus TO A NAMED SKILL, which is not a bucket grant: it pays whatever bucket that skill's hits read. So the scope is the name, full stop. The category was never load-bearing — had his Liberation been named "Basic Attack ..." the same mis-lift would have accidentally WORKED, which is the tell. It happened to read 'liberation', which is the one bucket his Liberation does not read (the game tags that row's instances type 0, so the hit reads Basic Attack — a Liberation CAST dealing Basic-bucket damage, which is ordinary and correct, NOT a defect and NOT a tagging error). Both gates together therefore matched nothing and the effect paid zero even once triggered and stacked. AN EARLIER VERSION OF THIS NOTE called it the Aemeath contradiction in mirror image; that was WRONG. Hers is a GENUINE contradiction between two real statements (her kit says her Heavy Attacks are "considered Resonance Liberation DMG"); this is one statement plus a parser artifact. Only the remedy is shared. Curated rather than bound by the parser because resolveNameToKeys CANNOT reach this key, roster-wide: the main Liberation is keyed bare `liberation` on 30 resonators whose row label carries the skill's own name, so the name has no token to match. Unambiguous all the same — he has exactly one liberation key and its own row label is "Resonance Liberation: Rewritten in Winter's Margins" verbatim.

S6.1._wiredVia: 2026-10-02 (OPEN-ITEMS 2): the blocker recorded in _resolvedVia below was wrong on BOTH halves — the stack source is neither Tune Break nor unresolvable, and the #7 wiring it waited on is not needed. His Forte Circuit states the whole gauge in its own section: 'Casting any form of [Aureole of Execution] grants 1 of [Endnotes on the Endgame]', 'stacking up to 3 times', 'Casting [Rewritten in Winter’s Margins] or switching to another Resonator removes all stacks' — now RESOURCE_DEFS[1510]. MEASURED BEFORE THE FIX: this effect was entirely OFF (trigger 'unknown' resolves to no application), so an S6 build's Liberation dealt EXACTLY the same damage as an S2 one — perStack/maxStacks were corrected in 2026-07-31's increment 1 and nothing could ever read them. The trigger names the three Aureole FORMS and only those: Golden Reflux is the base Resonance Skill that Aureole REPLACES, while Golden Impale and Ichor Deposit are follow-ups a form spawns, not forms of it. Window 'persist' is safe BECAUSE the count is the gauge — the Liberation's own spendAll zeroes it, so the effect self-scopes to zero on every step after, exactly as Denia's per-Dark-Core multiplier does.
S6.1._resolvedVia: 2026-07-31 gauge-engine increment 1: 'Each stack of Endnotes on the Endgame additionally grants Resonance Liberation Rewritten in Winter's Margins 40% DMG Bonus, up to 120%.' pctNear() reads the first % AFTER the 'DMG Bonus' keyword and so captured the 120% CEILING as the per-stack value (1.20). The kit states 40% per stack to a 120% ceiling = 3 stacks. Stack source is Tune Break DMG dealt by teammates — unresolvable until OPEN-ITEMS #7 wires computeTuneBreakDamage.

S6.0._resolvedVia: 2026-10-02, found by tests/dead-scope.test.mjs: "The DMG Multiplier of Forte Circuit's Sweet Dream is additionally increased by 150%." shipped scoped to skillType 'forte' and therefore DEAD -- 'forte' is not an attribution tag AND nodeTypeMatches strips forte_ off the node type, so it matches nothing on either lens. The category was lifted from the NAME "Forte Circuit's Sweet Dream", the same false positive as Luuk Herssen S6.1. [Sweet Dream] is NOT a skill: it is a named buff inside [Budding Mode] -- "- [Sweet Dream]: Increase the DMG Multiplier of [Normal Attack], Basic Attack [Vining Waltz], Basic Attack [Blazing Waltz], Basic Attack [Vining Ronde], Dodge Counter [Atonement], Resonance Skill [Crimson Blossom], and Resonance Skill [Floral Ravage] by 50%." So this node is an ENHANCEMENT of that buff and carries ITS scope, which is why the nine keys here are copied verbatim from the base effect's own resolved skillKeys (skillNodeEffects[0].effects[0]) rather than re-derived -- Vining Waltz is a four-stage chain, which is why nine keys answer seven names. The state gate is the kit's own ("Camellya enters [Budding Mode] after casting [Ephemeral]", "[Budding Mode] ends when Camellya is switched off the field") and matches the S3.1 override above.
S6.0._asymmetryNote: The BASE effect it enhances sits in skillNodeEffects, which this file cannot address (slot namespaces are only S<level>.<index> and IH<node>.<index>), and its window is "seconds: 15" -- a number scraped from an unrelated clause of the same node desc ("Each bud lasts for 15s", the Crimson Bud lifetime; Budding Mode itself has NO timer). It is right by coincidence here: its trigger is exactly forte_heavy_ephemeral, the cast that ENTERS Budding Mode, so "15s after Ephemeral" tracks the state across her six-step tail -- MEASURED active on exactly steps 11-16, the Budding Mode steps, and on no others. This override uses the real state gate instead, so on a tail longer than 15s the enhancement would stay live after the base expired. The base is the wrong half there (Budding Mode does not expire), and no shipped rotation reaches it.

S5.0._resolvedVia: 2026-10-02, found by tests/dead-scope.test.mjs: "The damage of Forte Circuit Power Shift is increased by 50%." shipped scoped to skillType 'forte' and therefore DEAD on BOTH lenses -- 'forte' is not an attribution tag, and nodeTypeMatches strips forte_ off the NODE type, so 'forte' is compared against 'heavy' and never matches. The category was lifted from the NAME "Forte Circuit Power Shift", the same false positive as Luuk Herssen S6.1 and Camellya S6.0. POWER SHIFT IS THE FORTE CIRCUIT NODE'S OWN NAME, not a skill, and the game says so structurally rather than by inference: skill_trees[7].skill is NAMED "Power Shift", its desc describes Timed Counters, and its own level params are exactly "Timed Counters Stage 1/2/3 DMG" plus "Timed Counters Stage 1/2/3 Shield" -- a direct parent/child relation. Two further witnesses agree: those three are her ONLY Forte Circuit damage rows (nothing else it could mean), and the sibling chain clause "Forte Circuit Power Shift's Shield is increased by 40%" matches the Shield params of that same node. Unconditional, so trigger/window are left as parsed (none/always); the NAME scope is what satisfies the unscoped-multiplierUp danger.

S2.1._resolvedVia: 2026-09-21 (OPEN-ITEMS 33): full text 'The DMG Multiplier of Scarlet Coda is increased by 75%. Aftersound now additionally increases the DMG Multiplier of Scarlet Coda by 75%.' S2.0 (the first sentence) is the flat, always-on +75% and is correctly unconditional. S2.1 (this slot) names Aftersound — her stacking gauge (inherentSkills 'Octet': 10 stacks entering combat, +2.5% Crit. DMG/stack) — as the SOURCE of the second +75%, which the classifier could not read as a gate: the clause uses the resource as its grammatical SUBJECT ('Aftersound now additionally increases…') rather than a 'while'/'when' phrase, so classifyCondition fell through to 'unconditional' and both +75% grants applied every hit, unconditionally, doubling to +150% — the same wielder-always shape the unscoped-multiplierUp invariant warns about. Not modelled as a real gate here: Aftersound has no RESOURCE_DEFS entry, so the exact threshold (any stack vs. a stated minimum) is not derivable from this text alone. Turned OFF by default (situational/unknown/persist, the same shape used elsewhere for an un-modelled state gate) rather than left doubled — this is the safe direction: understating a real conditional bonus, not crediting an unconditional one the kit never grants. A user can still toggle it on in the build editor; a future Aftersound RESOURCE_DEFS entry could resolve the trigger properly.

S3.1._resolvedVia: 2026-07-05: misparse, not a self-buff at all. Full text: 'Targets hit by Enhanced Attack - Hecate: Cadenza will have their ATK reduced by 20% for 15s.' — an ENEMY ATK debuff, parsed as a self atkRatio buff. This engine doesn't model incoming-damage-taken (enemy ATK is not a resonator stat), so the effect is out of scope, not a fixable trigger/window — suppressed rather than misapplied as a +20% self ATK buff.

IH0.0._resolvedVia: 1-3 stacks of Havoc Bane, 10% amplify per stack, up to 30%. 2026-08-01, corrected: Havoc Bane's BASE cap of 3 (enemy-status.js NEGATIVE_STATUS_DEFS) is RIGHT. The 4-6 band is reachable because Yangyang: Xuanling RAISES it herself - S3: 'After casting Intro Skill - Skybound Feather, Resonance Skill - Sword Stance Flow: Azure, or Resonance Skill - Sword Stance Flow: Feather, increase the maximum Havoc Bane stacks on targets within a certain range by 3, lasting 20s.' Per-kit cap raises are a general mechanic (Cartethyia S2 +3 Aero Erosion, Suisui +3 Electro Flare, Aemeath S6 Fusion/Rupturous Trail), not modelled yet - OPEN-ITEMS #25. IH0.0 and IH0.1 are the two BANDS of one piecewise function and are mutually exclusive by stack count, so each carries a stackBand and scaleEffect zeroes the branch that does not match. Window is always/trigger none because the CONDITION IS THE BAND: the effect applies whenever the target holds a Havoc Bane count inside it, which stackBand already gates. Left as persist+unknown the pair was not double-counting - it was entirely INERT (isEffectOnAtStep resolves persist+unknown to OFF), so the amplify never applied at all.

_deferredDoc: Read by tools/effect-audit.js only (NOT merged by preprocess.mjs — these effects stay unresolved/OFF in the sim). Tracks ⚠ entries that are explicitly accepted as deferred rather than fixed, so the audit gate stays honest about what's deliberately postponed vs. what still needs a decision. Keyed deferred.<resonatorId>.<slotKey> -> reason string.

1102.S3.0: "Sanhua's damage dealt is increased by 35% against targets with HP below 70%." Gated on the TARGET's remaining HP, which the sim does not model at all — there is no enemy HP pool, only a damage total. Resolves OFF via the situational classifier, which is the honest read; a fight-long +35% would be the alternative. Deferred 2026-08-07 by the buff-coverage pass, which is what made the clause parse at all.

1108.IH0.0: Snow Rust 3-stack tier, newly parsed by the 2026-08-07 buff-coverage pass ("Glacio Bite DMG is Amplified by 30%"). Already SUPPRESSED via overrides.1108.IH0.0 — distinctApplicatorTierContribution (conditional-buffs.js) owns the whole tier ladder — so the effect exists in the dataset for display but must never be applied twice. Deferred here so the audit gate sees the decision rather than an undecided flag.
1108.S3.1: Snow Rust tiered unlock (chain modification of IH0's tiered unlock) — chain effects stay display-only per CLAUDE.md (bespoke per character, not mechanically applied), unlike IH0 itself which is now resolved via distinctApplicatorTierContribution (conditional-buffs.js), see overrides.1108.IH0.*. Deferred 2026-06-27; resolution scope narrowed 2026-06-28.
1108.S6.1: Same Snow Rust mechanic (chain modification of IH0's tiered unlock). Deferred 2026-06-27, same reason as S3.1. Renumbered from S6.0 on 2026-08-07: S6 gained a leading effect once the +500% Crit. DMG clause became readable (the game scopes it by BulletIds, see data/buff-facts.json), which shifted every slot below it by one.

1205.IH0.0: Fusion DMG Bonus (5%/stack of Enflamement, correctly extracted, but maxStacks not captured — should be 4, matching Enflamement's own cap) only applies to the SAME True Sight Conquest/Charge cast that's currently active, scaled by Enflamement at that moment — not a time-windowed buff. Per maintainer 2026-06-27: 'elementBonus is always global, never skill-specific — for that, skill-type-specific buffs exist', but the current schema has no 'instantaneous, scoped to the exact step that fired it, stack-scaled' bonus kind either (skillTypeBonus is duration/window-based once active, same as everything else). Needs a new resolution kind: apply only to the damage instance of the triggering cast itself. Maintainer flagged the source text as 'a bit murky' on exactly how it composes with simultaneous DMG instances. Deferred 2026-06-27.
1205.IH1.0: Same instantaneous/non-windowed gap as IH0.0 (applies only to the same Heavy Attack Flaming Sacrifice / Liberation cast that fires it, not a duration buff). ADDITIONALLY: the extracted value (0.15) is WRONG — pctNear() grabbed the trailing '15%' from '...ignores 15% of the target's DEF' instead of the actual '20% Fusion DMG Bonus' earlier in the same sentence (DMG Bonus keyword match position is between the two numbers; pctNear only scans forward). The DEF-ignore 15% is also an entirely separate, currently unextracted effect (a defShred-type bonus, not elementBonus) bundled in the same source sentence. Do not reuse 0.15 as the Fusion DMG Bonus value when this is eventually built — it should be 0.20, plus a new sibling DEF-ignore effect at 0.15. Deferred 2026-06-27.

1211.S3.1: "When the number of Dark Cores reaches the limit, casting Basic Attack - Stagecraft Form Stage 4 or Resonance Skill Phantom Bubble - Stagecraft Form consumes all Dark Cores and increases the DMG Multiplier of this skill by 1200%." Two things block it: Dark Cores are a resource gauge the sim does not track, and "this skill" names neither of the two casts it could be, so skill-scope.mjs has nothing to bind. Resolves OFF. Deferred 2026-08-07.

1506.S2.1: "When in Confession, Silent Prayer grants 120% more DMG Amplification for Spectro Frazzle." The amplify lands on the STATUS's damage, not on Phoebe's hits — a different formula entirely (enemy-status.js has no crit and no gear stat). Applying it as a Spectro amplify on her skills would be a 120% error in her favour. Belongs to the affliction-damage lane. Deferred 2026-08-07.

1607.IH1.0: "Casting Echo Skill gives 6% Havoc DMG Bonus for 10s, stacking up to 2 times." The trigger is a real cast, but an Echo Skill emits no phrase type — phraseTypesForStep (sim.js) has no 'echo' branch, so no castMatch trigger can ever see one. Resolving it needs the echo cast wired into the trigger vocabulary, which is its own change. Deferred 2026-08-07.

1509.S3.1: Premixed Hue stacks are driven by a continuous 'Lumiflow' resource gauge (gain 1 stack/1s in combat or /0.5s out of combat while Lumiflow >= 120, lose stacks below that threshold, reset to 0 when Additive Color ends, max 25) — no time-based threshold-gated resource gauge exists in the engine. Different in kind from a discrete castMatch trigger; needs the same class of new infra as Hiyuki's Snow Rust (a continuous-resource accumulator), not a one-line override. Deferred 2026-06-27.
